blocks.text: Port Kells Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: Port Kells splits at Highway 1: the industrial area sits north of it by the Fraser River, and the house streets sit south of it toward the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR).

The Anniedale-Tynehead Neighbourhood Concept Plan (NCP) area, the planned part of south Port Kells, covers about 408 hectares (ha), bounded by Highway 1 and 96 Avenue north, 168 Street west, the ALR south and Harvie Road east.
176 Street (Highway 15) is the area's north-south truck route, and 88 Avenue is the east-west street carrying Port Kells Elementary at 19076 88 Avenue.

blocks.text: Port Kells Houses: the housing stock

items.t: Houses here are mostly on acreage lots: the City first described Anniedale-Tynehead as rural acreage lots and agricultural uses, now designated to support urban development.

Surrey Zoning By-law No. 12000 zone names for this stock include RA (One-Acre Residential), RH (Half-Acre Residential) and A-1 (General Agriculture), per the Development Cost Charge (DCC) bylaw zone list.
North of Highway 1 the stock changes completely: the Port Kells industrial area spans 781 acres and is primarily zoned for light industrial use.

blocks.text: Port Kells Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The ALR edge is the controlling line: the NCP plan area stops at the ALR in the south, so a lot's ALR status decides whether farm rules or the NCP govern it.
Protected watercourses cross the plan area, including the Serpentine River and several tributaries, and the City calls them significant and protected.

blocks.text: Port Kells Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Port Kells Elementary opened in 1907, and the first Port Kells school opened in 1891 on the Telegraph Trail, then inside Langley's boundaries.
The Serpentine River is controlled by a sea dam at King George Highway, first built in the 1912-1913 period with the Nicomekl dam, to keep salt water out of farm irrigation.
South Port Kells was only picked for new development in 2003, with a General Land Use Plan approved in 2005, which is why the house streets still read rural.
The plan area is expected to hold up to 20,000 Surrey residents once built out, on gently sloping highlands above the agricultural lowlands.
The industrial area's 2025 DCC schedule has separate Port Kells industrial and commercial rates, a cost signal that the north side is planned as employment land.

blocks.text: Port Kells Houses: development and new projects

items.t: Anniedale-Tynehead NCP, bounded by Highway 1, 168 Street, the ALR and Harvie Road, City of Surrey, mixed residential and employment plan area, about 408 ha. Status: Stage 1 endorsed September 2024; Stage 2 servicing and financial planning underway (as of November 3, 2026).

blocks.text: Port Kells Houses: costs and taxes

items.t: Port Kells carries its own DCC geography: the City's DCC bylaw lists the Anniedale-Tynehead and Port Kells industrial areas as separate charge areas from general Surrey zones.
Acreage lots under the RA and RH zones are charged DCCs by zone at subdivision, so a split on 88 Avenue prices differently from an RF-zone lot elsewhere in Surrey.

blocks.text: Port Kells Houses: getting around

items.t: Highway 1 and 176 Street (Highway 15) do the heavy lifting: the NCP area is bounded by Highway 1 and 96 Avenue in the north, so most trips start at those two interchanges.
Trails are part of the plan, not an afterthought: the NCP network links neighbourhood parks, schools and Tynehead Regional Park, with an overpass connection across Highway 1 toward Fraser Heights.

blocks.text: Port Kells Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check ALR status before any farm-use assumption: the NCP boundary uses the ALR as its south edge, and lots can sit on either side of that line on the same street.
